nodes.summary: `max(Z, 0)²` has the mixture law `½ δ₀ + ½ χ²₁` (chi-bar-square with weights `½, ½`).
nodes.title: Law of the positive part squared of a standard normal variable

nodes.summary: If `Y ~ N(0, v)` with `v ≠ 0`, then `Y² / v ~ χ²₁`.
nodes.title: Squared normalized Gaussian is chi-square with one degree of freedom

nodes.summary: As `tendstoInDistribution_scoreStatistic`, with `I(θ₀)` replaced by any estimators `Î n` converging to `I(θ₀)` in probability. Where `Î n ω = 0` the statistic takes Lean's value `x / 0 = 0`; this event has probability tending to `0` because `0 < I(θ₀)`.
nodes.title: Rao's score test with an estimated information

nodes.summary: Under the conditions of `tendstoInDistribution_score` and `0 < I(θ₀)`, the score statistic `(n^{-1/2} ∑_{i<n} score p θ₀ (X i))² / I(θ₀)` converges in distribution to `χ²₁`.
nodes.title: Rao's score test, known information

nodes.summary: If moreover `θ̂ₙ ω` maximizes the log-likelihood `ℓₙ θ = ∑_{i<n} log p θ (X i ω)` over all `θ` for every `n` and `ω`, then the likelihood-ratio statistic `2 (sup_θ ℓₙ θ - ℓₙ θ₀)` converges in distribution to `χ²₁`.
nodes.title: Wilks' theorem, supremum form

nodes.summary: Likelihood ratio on the boundary (one-sided parameter space `θ ∈ [0, ∞)`, true value `θ₀ = 0`). Let the model be defined and regular on a ball about `0` as in `tendstoInDistribution_two_mul_logLikelihood_sub` (so `0` is interior to the domain of the family, though not to the parameter space), and let `θ̂ₙ` be a consistent root of the likelihood equation. The statistic `2 (ℓₙ(max θ̂ₙ 0) - ℓₙ(0))` of the estimator…
nodes.title: Likelihood ratio on the boundary

nodes.summary: Under the conditions of `tendstoInDistribution_waldStatistic` and joint measurability of `(θ, x) ↦ p θ x`, the log-likelihood-ratio statistic `2 (ℓₙ(θ̂ₙ) - ℓₙ(θ₀))`, `ℓₙ θ = ∑_{i<n} log p θ (X i)`, of a consistent root `θ̂ₙ` of the likelihood equation converges in distribution to `χ²₁`.
nodes.title: Wilks' theorem (simple null)

nodes.summary: As `tendstoInDistribution_waldStatistic`, with `I(θ₀)` replaced by any estimators `Î n → I(θ₀)` in probability (for example the observed information of `tendstoInMeasure_observedInformation`; `I(θ̂ₙ)` also qualifies when `θ ↦ I(θ)` is continuous at `θ₀`, by the continuous mapping theorem).
nodes.title: Wald's test with an estimated information

nodes.summary: Under the conditions of `tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_mul_sub_of_likelihoodEquation` (without the normalization `∫ p θ dν = 1`, which that proof does not use), the Wald statistic `n (θ̂ₙ - θ₀)² I(θ₀)` of a consistent root `θ̂ₙ` of the likelihood equation converges in distribution to `χ²₁`.
nodes.title: Wald's test

nodes.summary: For i.i.d. observations with law `p θ₀ ν`, if `∂_θ score p θ₀` is measurable and integrable with `E ∂_θ score p θ₀ = -I(θ₀)` (the information identity), then `-(1/n) ∑_{i<n} ∂_θ score p θ₀ (X i) → I(θ₀)` in probability.
nodes.title: Consistency of the observed information

nodes.summary: Let `θ̂ₙ` be `√n`-consistent (`√n (θ̂ₙ - θ₀)` converges in distribution) and solve the likelihood equation with probability tending to one. nodes.title: Quadratic expansion of the log-likelihood ratio

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
